mainTopic: Brothers confirming a שטר's signatures, and the new משנה on which uses of a courtyard create a חזקה, with the גמרא's search for the reason
overview: The גמרא tells of a שטר signed by two witnesses, one of whom died. The living witness's brother and another person came to confirm the dead witness's signature. רבינא compares this to the earlier משנה of three brothers who each testify together with an outsider. רב אשי rejects the comparison: here brothers would supply three-quarters of the testimony, which is not allowed. A new משנה then lists casual uses of a courtyard that do not create a חזקה, such as keeping an animal or an oven there. It also lists built setups that do create one, such as a ten-טפחים partition or a proper manure pit. The גמרא asks why the two halves differ. עולא answers that a חזקה works like acquiring the property of a גר who died without heirs. רב ששת disproves this with plowing and eating produce. The גמרא then begins a new answer from רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A document whose second witness died
steps.stepSummary: A שטר had two witness signatures. One witness died. The living witness's brother and an outsider came to confirm the dead witness's signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a document signed by two witnesses, and one of them died. The brother of the surviving witness, together with one other person, came to testify that the dead witness's signature was real.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a real case about confirming the signatures on a document. This sets up the question of whether this way of confirming them is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make a שטר usable in court, its signatures must be confirmed. The living witness can confirm his own signature, but the dead witness's signature needs two other people. The problem is that one of those two is the living witness's own brother, and relatives cannot testify together.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document, such as a loan document

phrases.english: A certain document
that had two people signed on it,
one of them died.
The brother of the one who was still alive came,
and one other person,
to testify about the signature of the other one.
phrases.notes: The other one is the witness who died. The living witness confirms his own signature himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שְׁטָרָא דַּהֲוָה חֲתִימִי עֲלֵיהּ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case connected to the earlier משנה about brothers testifying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case presented: the living witness's brother and an outsider testify about the dead witness's signature.

steps.title: רבינא compares the case to the three brothers in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא wanted to say this case matches the משנה of three brothers who each join with an outsider, so the testimony should be valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא thought to say: this is just like our משנה, which teaches that three brothers can testify, with one other person joining each of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tries to use the earlier משנה to show that the brother's testimony here is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, each brother testified about a different year together with an outsider, and that was accepted. רבינא sees the same pattern here: each brother is part of a separate testimony. One confirms his own signature, and the other confirms the dead witness's signature together with an outsider.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a view that will be rejected)
Joins together with, to make a complete pair of witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase סבר למימר tells you that רבינא's comparison is about to be rejected. It is not the final word.

phrases.english: Ravina thought to say:
This is the same as our Mishnah:
phrases.notes: He means the earlier משנה about witnesses for the three years of owning land.

phrases.english: three brothers, and one other person joins with them.
phrases.notes: Each brother testifies about one year, with the outsider as the second witness each time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source-based ruling for the case in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the brother's testimony on the dead witness's signature is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of three brothers each joined by one outsider

steps.title: רב אשי: here three-quarters of the testimony comes from brothers
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the comparison. In the משנה, brothers never supply three-quarters of the testimony, but here they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Are these cases really alike? There, three-quarters of the money is not taken away based on the word of brothers. Here, three-quarters of the money is taken away based on the word of brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the two cases are different, so רבינא's proof falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Count each signature as half the proof. The living witness confirms his own signature, which is one half. His brother supplies half of the confirmation of the other signature, which is another quarter. So brothers provide three-quarters of the testimony. In the משנה, each brother supplies only half of each year's testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: On the word (literally 'on the mouth') of

steps.whatToRemember: Relatives cannot make up most of a testimony. If brothers end up supplying three-quarters of the proof for a שטר, the confirmation does not work.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him:
Are they comparable?!
There, what is taken out is not
the money minus a quarter
on the word of brothers;
here, what is taken out is
the money minus a quarter
on the word of brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי מִי דָּמֵי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the שטר case and the three-brothers משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the שטר case, brothers supply three-quarters of the testimony. In the משנה, they never do.

steps.title: New משנה: uses of a courtyard that do not create a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks which uses create a חזקה. It lists casual uses of a courtyard that do not: keeping an animal, an oven, a millstone or a stove there, raising chickens, or putting manure there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which things create a חזקה, and which do not? If someone kept an animal in a courtyard, or an oven, a millstone or a stove, or raised chickens there, or put his manure in the courtyard, this is not a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It first lists uses of a courtyard that are not strong enough to show ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are loose, everyday uses with no fixed structure. Because of that, the other owner of the courtyard would not feel he needs to protest. So they do not serve as proof of ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
A use of property that proves ownership

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Which are the things that create a presumption of ownership,
and which are the things that do not create a presumption of ownership?
If one would keep an animal in a courtyard;
or an oven, a millstone, or a stove;
or raises chickens;
or puts his manure in the courtyard –
it is not a presumption of ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Casual uses of a courtyard (animal, oven, millstone, stove, chickens, manure) do not create a חזקה.

steps.title: Uses with a built structure do create a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: Building a ten-טפחים partition for an animal, oven, stove or millstone does create a חזקה. So does bringing chickens into the house, or making a manure pit or mound three טפחים deep or high.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he built a partition ten handbreadths high for his animal, and the same for the oven, the stove and the millstone; or brought chickens into the house; or made a place for his manure three handbreadths deep or three handbreadths high, this is a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by listing the stronger uses that do count as proof of ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change from step 4 is a fixed, built setup: a real partition, a set place, or a proper pit or mound. A permanent setup like this is something the other owner would protest if it were not allowed. That is why it counts as a חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: Casual use of a courtyard is not a חזקה. A permanent, built setup, such as a ten-טפחים partition or a three-טפחים manure pit or mound, is a חזקה.

phrases.english: But if he made a partition for his animal –
ten handbreadths high,
and likewise for the oven, and likewise for the stove,
and likewise for the millstone;
or he brought chickens into the house;
or he made a place for his manure –
three handbreadths deep or three handbreadths high;
this is a presumption of ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting cases to step 4: built setups that do create a חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ten-טפחים partition, bringing chickens into the house, or a three-טפחים manure pit or mound creates a חזקה.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two halves of the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the casual uses in the first clause do not create a חזקה, while the built-up uses in the second clause do.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first clause, and what is different about the latter clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's split: why is keeping an animal in the courtyard not enough, but building a partition for it is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both clauses talk about the same kinds of uses: animals, ovens, millstones, chickens and manure. The only difference is whether something was built or made. The גמרא wants the principle that explains why that difference matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is different? A request for the reason two cases are treated differently
The first clause of the משנה
The latter clause of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different in the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is from Step 4: just keeping an animal, oven and so on there does not create a חזקה.

phrases.english: and what is different in the latter clause?
phrases.notes: The latter clause is from Step 5: building a partition or making a pit does create a חזקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the distinction in the משנה just quoted in Steps 4 and 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains why casual use does not create a חזקה but building a partition or making a pit does.

steps.title: עולא: a חזקה works the same way as acquiring ownerless property
steps.stepSummary: עולא says any act that would acquire the property of a גר who died without heirs also creates a חזקה on another person's property, and any act that would not, does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: Any act which, if done on the property of a גר, would acquire it, also acquires on another person's property. Any act which, if done on the property of a גר, would not acquire it, also does not acquire on another person's property.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by linking חזקה to the rules for taking ownerless property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To take ownerless property you need an act done to the land itself, like building. Simply having an animal stand there is not such an act. So the first clause does not create a חזקה, while building a partition, which would acquire ownerless land, does.

keyTerms.meaning: Property of a convert who died without heirs, which becomes ownerless and anyone can take it
He acquired. Here it means the act counts for ownership or a חזקה
Another person's property, where the question is whether a חזקה is created

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a single test that explains the whole משנה: compare the act to what works for ownerless property.

phrases.english: Ulla says:
Any act which, if done on a convert's property, would acquire it –
phrases.notes: This is a גר who died with no Jewish heirs, so his property is ownerless and up for grabs.

phrases.english: acquires on another person's property,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאִילּוּ בְּנִכְסֵי הַגֵּר לֹא קָנָה –
phrases.english: any act which, if done on a convert's property, would not acquire it –
does not acquire on another person's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6 by giving a general rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חזקה is created only by an act that would acquire ownerless property (נכסי הגר). Casual use would not, and building would.

steps.title: רב ששת: plowing and eating produce break the rule
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת shows two cases where the rule fails. Plowing acquires a convert's property but does not create a חזקה on someone else's. Eating the produce creates a חזקה on someone else's property but does not acquire a convert's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: Is this really a rule? But there is plowing, which acquires the property of a גר but does not acquire another person's property! And there is eating the produce, which acquires another person's property but does not acquire the property of a גר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks עולא's rule by giving one counter-example in each direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the two kinds of acquiring always match. Plowing works for ownerless property but not for a חזקה. Eating the produce for three years is the classic חזקה, yet it does not acquire ownerless property. So the two systems do not line up, and the rule falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, a strong challenge to a statement
Plowing or breaking up the soil
Eating the produce of the field, the standard way of making a חזקה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the two counter-examples make the same point. They go in opposite directions: plowing works only for ownerless property, and eating produce works only for a חזקה.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objects to this:
And is this a rule?!
But there is plowing –
which acquires on a convert's property,
but does not acquire on another person's property!
And there is eating the produce –
which acquires on another person's property,
but does not acquire on a convert's property!

steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that acquiring ownerless property and making a חזקה always work through the same acts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two counter-examples in opposite directions: plowing works for נכסי הגר but not for a חזקה, and eating produce works for a חזקה but not for נכסי הגר. So the two do not match.

steps.title: A new explanation begins from רב נחמן quoting רבה בר אבוה
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting עולא's rule, the גמרא introduces a different answer in the name of רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה. The content comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said that רבה בר אבוה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. The word אלא shows that עולא's approach is dropped and a new explanation of the משנה is about to be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב ששת showed that עולא's rule does not hold, the original question from Step 6 is open again. Only the speakers are named here, and their actual explanation follows next.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman said
that Rabba bar Avuh said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops עולא's rejected answer and opens a new answer to the question of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement answer: a new explanation of the משנה instead of עולא's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The distinction in the משנה could be explained by comparing it to acquiring ownerless property, as עולא said.
steps.terutzMaskana: That comparison fails, so a different explanation from רבה בר אבוה is about to be given.
